source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Durham campus is the largest disclosed data center load in North Carolina, and it is 80 percent of everything the state has published.

The campus carries 40 MW of published IT capacity across DUR1 and DUR2, with 420,000 square feet of technical space. North Carolina has 19 mapped facilities, but 14 publish no capacity at all. So the state's real inventory is unknown, and the one number that is known dominates the disclosed total by default rather than by comparison. A single operator's spec page is doing most of the work of describing the state's compute footprint.

For AI specifically, the disclosed figure is a floor on electrical demand, not a measure of what the site can train. The operator publishes no breakdown by workload or tenant class, so the 40 MW could serve general colocation or dense training and the data cannot distinguish between them. The rack and accelerator estimates in the reading are arithmetic on assumed densities, not operator disclosures, and should be read as such.

What is missing matters more than what is present. There is no stated power infrastructure, no PUE, no grid operator for Durham, and no power purchase agreements. Without those, nothing here establishes whether the 40 MW can run continuously, at what utilization, or against what supply constraint. The absence of certifications is likewise a gap in the record, not evidence that none exist.
